topic: Marsa El Brega LNG nameplate capacity — conflicting source figures
wiki_text: Capacity for the Marsa El Brega (Marsa el-Brega) LNG plant is reported inconsistently across sources. The facility comprises four liquefaction trains, built by Esso (Exxon) and operating since 1970 — the third LNG export terminal built in the world. Reported total/per-train figures: (a) Oil & Gas Journal: four 750,000-tpy trains = ~3.0 mtpa total; (b) Energy Intelligence: original per-train nameplate ~700,000 tpy (~2.8 mtpa total), with a Shell/NOC revamp target of 3.2 mtpa (4.4 bcm/y) under the 2005-2008 upgrade scheme; recent supply before mothballing was only ~490,000 tpy. Sanctions in the 1980s-90s and under-investment cut output to ~15% of nameplate, and the plant was severely damaged in the civil war (mothballed since ~2011; no LNG-export restart as of 2026). GEM records 4 x 0.80 mtpa = 3.2 mtpa, which matches the Energy Intelligence revamp target rather than the historical nameplate. The Shell/NOC revamp (announced 2005, agreement 2008; Shell committed $105m-$450m) never materialized.

topic: Operator / ownership and recent (non-LNG) Brega activity
wiki_text: Marsa El Brega LNG is owned/operated by Sirte Oil Company (full name: Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company, formed 1981), an owned subsidiary of Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) whose remit per NOC includes oil/gas exploration and production, natural gas liquefaction, crude refining, and methanol. Recent activity at Brega has been LPG / gas-distribution / pipeline logistics rather than LNG export — e.g., reports of LPG tanker calls and a trial run of a ~42-inch gas pipeline (Intisar A/103 to the Brega network) recovering previously flared gas — and should not be misread as an LNG-export restart. GEM's owner (Sirte Oil Co) and parent (National Oil Corp) are correct.
